core_obligations: Part (1): from compositions $h_i : X_i \to Y$ having $\mathcal{P}$ along a smooth covering of $X$, produce for each $x$ a smooth morphism of pairs $(X_i, x_i) \to (X, x)$ and use definition part (3) with $\mathrm{id}_Y$; converses by definition part (1) (proof lines 2906-2919).

Part (2): from base changes $h_i : X_i \to Y_i$ having $\mathcal{P}$ along a smooth covering of $Y$, produce the smooth morphism of pairs $(X_i, x_i) \to (X, x)$ and use definition part (3); converses by definition part (2) (proof lines 2919-2932).
Part (3): for $f$ with $\mathcal{P}$ and $g : Y \to Z$ smooth, use the identity morphism of pairs on $(X, x)$ with $g$ smooth to match definition part (3) (proof lines 2932-2943).
proof_roadmap: Prove locality on the source by feeding covering data into part (3) of the definition.
Prove locality on the target the same way with base-changed data.
Prove stability under smooth postcomposition with the identity pair.
difficulty_reason: The author announces 'We write everything out completely' and does: each of the three consequences is proved by producing the required morphism of pairs (with $\mathrm{id}_Y$, the chart map, or the identity on $(X,x)$) matching part (3) of the definition, plus the definition's own parts (1) and (2) for the converse directions.
